column4: Welcome to {INN}. Ale, bread, a bench by the fire - what'll it be?
Shut the door behind you, the draught eats my fire. Now, what can I pour you?
Coin first, talk after. That's the rule in {INN}. What are you drinking?
Mind your sword in here. We've had soldiers through all week and I'm short two stools already.
Come in out of the cold. There's mulled ale on the hearth, if you've the coin.
Stamp the snow off your boots. Ale's brown, the stew's hot, and nobody asks your business.
Sit where you like, only not by the old man at the fire. That's been his seat since before the last winter.
Winter's teeth are out tonight. A cup of something hot, friend?
Salt on your cloak and coin in your fist, I hope. What will it be?
Good day to you. The wine comes up from the Reach, the ale is our own. Which will you have?
Welcome, welcome. Summerwine or ale - we have the one in plenty and the other in better plenty.
Another traveller on the road. Sit, eat, keep your head down - these days that's the best advice in the riverlands.
If you've come to burn us out, you're late, someone did it last spring. If you've come to drink, sit down.
You've come down from the high road? Then you've earned a cup. What'll it be?
Hang your cloak by the fire, the storms will have soaked you through. Ale or something stronger?
Fresh from the city or bound for it? Either way, you'll want a drink.
Out of the sun, friend. Our wine is red and strong, and the shade is free.
Come, come, sit. Wine from three cities and tales from nine. What will you have?
Ale's at the counter, love. Ask the keeper - he counts every drop.
Mind the floor, it's wet. Someone's always spilling something in here.
If you want a bed, it's the keeper you want. If you want gossip, it's the drovers by the fire.
Three lots of soldiers this month, and not one of them paid for their own cup.
Keep your hands to yourself and your boots near the fire, and we'll get on fine.
Don't sit by the window. Things come through windows these days.
You look thirsty. Everyone who comes in off that road looks thirsty.
The keeper says I'm to smile at every traveller. There. Now go and pay him.
We play for the room. A coin in the cup keeps the strings in tune.
A request? We know a dozen songs, and half of them are even decent.
Hush now, we're between songs. The next one is sad, so drink first.
We've a song about a winter that lasted a lifetime. It goes on a bit, like the winter.
We don't sing the war songs here. Folk have heard enough of the real thing.
A love song, a drinking song or a song about a knight? We do all three at once, if you pay double.
